clue.text: Business to come in with force

parts.note: to enter is to come in
to prise something is to force it open with leverage

explanation.surface: A firm muscling its way into a market by sheer force.
explanation.definitionFit: An enterprise is a company or commercial undertaking, a synonym for a business.

clue.text: Shoe seller paid badly

indicators.note: something done badly is botched, so the letters of the two words come out jumbled

parts.note: the two words taken as written supply the letters to shuffle

explanation.surface: A footwear vendor who has been paid poorly for their goods.
explanation.definitionFit: An espadrille is a light canvas shoe with a rope sole, one particular kind of footwear.

clue.text: Pull part of body by one's ear?

indicators.note: judging by ear means going by sound, so the word for the body part is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: a toe is one small part of the body

explanation.surface: Someone being dragged along by the ear like a naughty child.
explanation.definitionFit: To tow is to haul a vehicle or boat along behind, a synonym for pull.

clue.text: Cheese on toast, uncooked part

parts.note: rare meat is barely cooked, close to uncooked
a bit is a part or piece

explanation.surface: A snack where the cheese on top is partly raw, not properly grilled.
explanation.walkthrough: Welsh rarebit is the traditional British name for melted seasoned cheese on toast.
explanation.definitionFit: Rarebit, or Welsh rarebit, is the dish of melted cheese poured over toasted bread.

clue.text: Regret placing limits on price in landlord's payment

indicators.note: together with in, placing tells you to put one piece inside another
the edges of price go in the middle of the payment word

parts.note: rent is what a tenant pays the landlord

indicators.note: the limits of a word are its outer edges, so only its first and last letters are used

parts.note: the word price taken as written, before its edges are picked

explanation.surface: A tenant regretting the cap placed on what the landlord can charge.
explanation.definitionFit: To repent is to feel sorrow or remorse for something done, a synonym for regret as a verb.

clue.text: Slovak nearly fluffed volley

indicators.note: to fluff something is to bungle it, so the remaining letters are scrambled
nearly the whole word means losing its last letter

parts.note: the word Slovak taken as written, to be shortened

explanation.surface: A Slovak tennis player who almost made a mess of a volley.
explanation.walkthrough: In the surface 'volley' is a tennis shot; the answer means a burst of gunfire.
explanation.definitionFit: A salvo is a simultaneous discharge of guns, which is one meaning of volley.

clue.text: Great money

definitions.meaning: first meaning: excellent, of the highest quality
second meaning: the currency of the United Kingdom, the pound

explanation.walkthrough: Read together it suggests a large sum; the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Sterling describes something of excellent character and also names British currency, as in pounds sterling.

clue.text: Knotted rope has secured wrist, primarily for control

indicators.note: the rope holds the next letter fast inside it
a knotted rope is twisted up, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: the word rope taken as written, to be knotted

indicators.note: primarily means first, so just the opening letter of wrist

parts.note: the word wrist supplies its opening letter

explanation.surface: Someone tied up with a rope knotted around the wrist to keep them under control.
explanation.definitionFit: Power is authority or command over others, a synonym for control as a noun.

clue.text: Dad with delayed sense of taste

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father
late means delayed or behind time

explanation.surface: A father whose ability to taste has come on only late in life.
explanation.definitionFit: Your palate is your ability to distinguish flavours, literally the roof of the mouth.

clue.text: Commercial centre in race for details on contract

indicators.note: the shopping centre goes inside the race word

parts.note: a sprint is a short fast race
a mall is a shopping centre

explanation.surface: A shopping centre caught up in a contest over the fine points of an agreement.
explanation.definitionFit: Small print is the easily overlooked conditions printed in tiny type in a legal agreement.

clue.text: Follow supreme being from the East

indicators.note: in an across answer, reading from the east means from right to left, so backwards

parts.note: God is the supreme being

explanation.surface: A devotee following a deity whose religion comes from the Orient.
explanation.definitionFit: To dog someone is to trail them persistently, as a hound would, so it means follow.

clue.text: Ultimately upstanding, awfully strange criminal

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so the last letter of upstanding

parts.note: the word upstanding supplies its final letter

indicators.note: done awfully means done badly, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: the word strange taken as written, to be jumbled

explanation.surface: An apparently upright citizen who turns out to be a peculiar crook after all.
explanation.definitionFit: A gangster is a member of an organised gang of violent lawbreakers, so a criminal.

clue.text: Unruly mob, round about end of morning: one of a pair beaten

indicators.note: an unruly mob is disorderly, so its letters are thrown into disorder
about signals that the round word is turned about and mixed with the rest

parts.note: the word mob taken as written, part of the letter pool
the word round taken as written, part of the letter pool

indicators.note: the end of morning is its final letter

parts.note: the word morning supplies its last letter

explanation.surface: A riotous crowd gathering late in the morning to beat someone up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beaten' suggests violence from the mob, but it refers to a percussion instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: Bongos come as a linked pair of small drums played with the hands, so each is one of a beaten pair.

clue.text: Light that is surrounding good egg

indicators.note: the two letters for that is go around the rest

parts.note: i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is
a nit is the egg of a louse

explanation.surface: Light that encloses a good egg, as if an egg were glowing in a warm lamp.
explanation.definitionFit: To ignite something is to set fire to it, which is the verb sense of light.

clue.text: Arduous and extremely unusual to get around Phil

indicators.note: the outer letters wrap around the name that follows
the extremes of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: the word unusual taken as written, before its ends are picked
the name Phil taken just as written

explanation.surface: Phil finds things hard going and very odd to navigate.
explanation.definitionFit: An uphill task is difficult and strenuous, like climbing a slope, so arduous.

clue.text: Piece of pottery one throws

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a jug, often earthenware, for pouring
second meaning: the baseball player who throws the ball to the batter

explanation.walkthrough: A potter also throws pots on a wheel, which makes the two halves look like one picture.
explanation.definitionFit: A pitcher is both a large jug for liquids and the player who delivers the ball in baseball.

clue.text: Usual standard, rubbish mimic

parts.note: par is the normal or expected level, as in up to par
rot means nonsense, rubbish

explanation.surface: A critic dismissing ordinary impressionists as worthless copycats.
explanation.definitionFit: To parrot is to repeat someone's words without understanding, as the bird does, so mimic.

clue.text: Despair, turning to healers

indicators.note: turning means changing round, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the two words taken as written supply the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A desperate patient finally seeking out faith healers.
explanation.definitionFit: To lose heart is an idiom for becoming discouraged and giving up hope, which is to despair.

clue.text: Greeting Underworld, Orpheus originally

parts.note: Hell is the underworld of the dead

indicators.note: originally means at the start, so the first letter

parts.note: the name Orpheus supplies its opening letter

explanation.surface: Orpheus of Greek myth arriving in the underworld and being greeted there.
explanation.walkthrough: Orpheus descended to the underworld to bring back his wife Eurydice, so the picture fits the myth.
explanation.definitionFit: Hello is the everyday word said when meeting someone, a common salutation.

clue.text: Space program ambitious, Gemini initially set back

indicators.note: set back means put in reverse, so the letters run the other way
initially means at the beginning, so the first letter of each word

explanation.surface: NASA's ambitious Gemini space programme suffering a setback.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Space' looks like part of the NASA story, but it means a gap.
explanation.definitionFit: A gap is an empty space or opening between two things.

clue.text: Chap, one chopping down tree

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an informal spelling of fellow, a man
second meaning: someone who fells trees, a lumberjack

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one man felling a tree; the two senses are separate words that share a spelling.
explanation.definitionFit: Feller is a colloquial form of fellow, a man, and also literally a person who fells timber.

clue.text: Capital city of Doha, noisy somewhat

indicators.note: somewhat means partly, so the answer is just a portion of these words

parts.note: the answer runs across the end of Doha and the start of noisy

explanation.surface: A remark that the Qatari capital Doha is rather noisy.
explanation.walkthrough: Doha is itself a capital, which tempts you to look for it, but the answer straddles the two words.
explanation.definitionFit: Hanoi is the capital city of Vietnam.

clue.text: Bother old horse

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to pester or harass someone
second meaning: an old or worn-out horse

explanation.walkthrough: Read together it sounds like annoying an aged animal; the two are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: To nag is to pester persistently, and a nag is also an aged, broken-down horse.

clue.text: Scottish river, just direct

parts.note: the Forth is a river in Scotland flowing into the Firth of Forth near Edinburgh
right means just or fair

explanation.surface: A Scottish river described as running straight ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: A forthright person is frank and outspoken, a synonym for direct in manner.
